newsitem.title: UK: Funds ready for 1997 dip into emerging mkts - poll.
newsitem.headline: Funds ready for 1997 dip into emerging mkts - poll.

text.p: Global investors believe most emerging economies will experience a resurgence of growth in 1997 with investors flagging Latin America and China as the biggest potential stories, a survey released on Wednesday shows.
Next year would herald the return to favour of most emerging economies among investors and more assets allocated to them, a report commissioned by consultants Burson-Marsteller said.

"While 1996 has so far proved disappointing for many markets, fund managers predict that on a regional basis all major emerging markets will simultaneously exhibit good rates of growth for the first time," Burson-Marsteller's Paul Philpotts said.

"We have been saying of Latin America for a long time that a fresh approach and new realism is apparent, the economies are being deregulated and this is good for economic progress in the long-term," one respondent, Douglas Adams of Templeton International, said.

Many institutions said they were positive about Brazil and Peru over the long term. Mexico was also a preferred market. "In China we are very struck by foreign shares trading more cheaply than their domestic counterparts which is a unique situation and an indicator of the value in China at the moment," said Templeton's Adam.
Burson-Marsteller said the handover of Hong Kong to China next year was not a major concern as fund managers believed a further opening of a potentially huge growth market was available in China.
Eastern Europe was seen as more expensive than at the beginning of the year, although many institutions said it still offered many good opportunities, particularly in Poland.

The Asia Pacific region was still widely seen as over-heated and expensive with the last quarter of 1996 likely to be difficult. It is also the most susceptible to downturns in economic cycles, respondents said.
"However, problems here were seen as cyclical and not structural, and the general perception is that the region will see a return to growth in 1997," it said.
"Indonesia is viewed positively over the long-term. Many institutions were negative on Thailand on the forward view," said the report.

The quarterly survey covers institutions which manage a total of $200 billion in emerging markets equities, nearly 60 percent of all portfolio investment into emerging markets from the developed world.
The sample covers institutions controlling 78 percent of the total value of the world's global equity funds, which is $35 billion of a total $45 billion.
